record.context_brief: symmetry type graphs of convex polytopes
record.original_question: Which symmetry type graphs occur among convex polytopes, both at the combinatorial level and at the geometric level?

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Which (combinatorial) symmetry type graphs occur among convex polytopes? Which geometric symmetry type graphs occur?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

A convex polytope P in Euclidean space is a bounded intersection of finitely many closed half-spaces; it has a face lattice F(P) consisting of its faces (vertices, edges, …, facets, together with the empty face and P itself) ordered by inclusion. A flag of P is a maximal chain in F(P): one face of each dimension from −1 to dim P, pairwise incident. For each i ∈ {0, 1, …, dim P − 1}, every flag Φ has a unique i-adjacent flag Φ^i, obtained by replacing the i-dimensional face of Φ by the unique other face of that dimension lying between the (i−1)- and (i+1)-faces of Φ.

The combinatorial automorphism group Γ(P) is the group of order-preserving bijections of F(P), and the geometric symmetry group G(P) is the group of Euclidean isometries of the ambient space that map P to itself. Both groups act on the set of flags of P. The combinatorial symmetry type graph T_c(P) is the edge-colored multigraph whose vertices are the Γ(P)-orbits of flags, and in which two orbits O and O' are joined by an edge of color i whenever some flag in O is i-adjacent to some flag in O' (loops of color i are allowed when O = O'); the resulting graph is properly i-edge-colored in the sense that each vertex is incident with exactly one edge or loop of each color i ∈ {0, …, dim P − 1}. The geometric symmetry type graph T_g(P) is defined analogously using the orbits of G(P) acting on flags.

Problem. Characterize precisely which finite edge-colored multigraphs arise as combinatorial symmetry type graphs T_c(P) of convex polytopes P, and which arise as geometric symmetry type graphs T_g(P) of convex polytopes P. Equivalently, give necessary and sufficient conditions on such a graph T (with edge colors in {0, 1, …, n−1}, each vertex incident with exactly one edge of each color, and satisfying the standard 2-factor commutativity required of flag-graph quotients) for the existence of an n-dimensional convex polytope P whose combinatorial (respectively geometric) symmetry type graph equals T.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed among open problems on k-orbit polytopes and remains open in general. Subsequent work (e.g., on 2-orbit and 3-orbit polyhedra and on prescribing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes) addresses related characterization questions but does not provide a full description of which symmetry type graphs—combinatorial or geometric—are realized by convex polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on k-orbit polytopes (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: 35 open problems are presented on combinatorial, geometric and algebraic aspects of k-orbit abstract polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: The question is part of a collection of open problems on k-orbit polytopes.

status_evidence.title: Convex Polytopes and Tilings with Few Flag Orbits (Matteo)
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of convex polytopes with small numbers of flag orbits; not all symmetry type graphs are realized.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are known for convex polytopes with few flag orbits; the general realization question is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Automorphism groups of 3-orbit polyhedra
status_evidence.snippet: Studies 3-orbit polyhedra, extending the analysis beyond k<3.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature continues to address particular cases rather than the full characterization.
